verdict.rationale: Phaser's source lives in the public phaserjs/phaser GitHub repo (phaser-gh-1, phaser-gh-2) and a runtime probe confirms the npm package is MIT-licensed (phaser-probe-rt-1), meaning developers can freely read, fork, and modify the full engine source when they hit a limitation like Arcade Physics' constraints (phaser-docs-24). Community posts also show developers building directly against the framework and hitting/working around its internals (phaser-comm-11, phaser-comm-12), implying source-level familiarity is common. Missing for 10: explicit docs citing the license file/terms, contribution guidelines, or a first-hand account of someone patching engine source to solve a problem.
